english: “Do we then abolish the law through faith? By no means — rather, we establish the law.” The law through Moses taught those from Israel to worship one God: “For the Lord,” it says, “your God is one Lord.” And God himself addressed them, saying: “You shall have no other gods besides me.”

Did faith toward Christ, then, move those called through it so that they no longer worship the one God by nature? Do we abolish a law that brings offerings to the one true God? “By no means,” he says, “rather, we establish the law.” So we approach Christ as God, lest we be charged with destroying the law — and rather be praised for establishing the law through faith.

About Abraham he says: “Before the God in whom he believed, who makes the dead alive and calls the things that are not as though they are.” So when the power to make the dead alive would fit no one else except the God by nature alone — and Christ also makes the corrupted alive through his own flesh, touching the dead and raising them — how is he not true God, who also gave others authority to raise the dead through his name?

“So, my brothers, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another, the one raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit for God.” We are put to death to the law by leaving its worship; we belong to another, the one raised from the dead — that is, to Christ — eager to follow his gospel decrees, so that we may bear fruit for God. The chief of the gospel decrees is faith toward him, and this fruit of ours is offered to Christ as to God.
notes_covered: Edd. ζωογονοῦντος vs C ζωοποιοῦντος — keep ζωοποιοῦντος with clean sense.

title: Spirit of God is Spirit of Christ; Word truly became human
english: So then: the one raised from the dead is God, because the Word became flesh.

“Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God dwells in you. If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, yet the Spirit is life because of righteousness. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also make your mortal bodies alive through his Spirit who dwells in you.”

See how clearly God’s Spirit is called Christ’s. But if Christ were only a human set apart on his own, merely having God’s Word dwelling in him, how would the divine Spirit be called his? Yet the Spirit is his own — therefore he is God, and not otherwise. For God’s Word did not come to be in a human in that way; rather, he truly became human while remaining God. Only so can the Father’s Spirit be understood as Christ’s Spirit.

“For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. You did not receive a spirit of slavery again to fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry, ‘Abba, Father.’” The blessed Paul writes: “Because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, ‘Abba, Father.’”

So if by the Son’s Spirit we have boldness to call God Father — enriched with the Spirit of the Son who is Son by nature and in truth — how is Christ not God? Not merely as he is thought a human like us, but as the Word became flesh and shared blood and flesh as we do.
“Who will separate us from the love of God? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or danger, or sword?”
notes_covered: Against ‘mere man indwelt by Word’ reading of Christ.

title: Love due to God given to Christ; Christ judges as God
english: The law through Moses was saying and making commandment: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” So when we bring to Christ himself that love most fitting for God — with all strength, and highest, even to soul and blood — who dares in vain to say he would not be God? The holy ones’ aim has not missed what is fitting in any way.

“For I am persuaded that neither death nor life nor angels nor rulers nor things present nor things to come nor powers nor height nor depth nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” If nothing at all can separate us from God’s love, and that love is practiced by us in Christ Jesus, how is Christ not clearly God? When we love him, we love the God of all. And if I say “Christ,” I mean the Word from God who has become human.

“For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ,” he says. We shall stand before Christ; for he will sit “on the throne of his glory,” judging “the world in righteousness” — and yet David says, “God is judge.” Therefore Christ is God.

“But I have written to you more boldly in part, as reminding you again, because of the grace given me by God that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus to the nations, priestly serving the gospel of God, so that the offering of the nations may become acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.” Those entrusted with the priestly work minister to God alone; for priests stand by
notes_covered: Love owed to God offered to Christ => Christ is God.

title: Paul ministers Christ’s gospel as God’s; churches of Christ
english: priests. See, then: the inspired Paul says grace was given him by God to be a minister of Christ Jesus and to serve as priest among the nations the gospel of Christ. Therefore Christ is God, if while proclaiming Christ to the nations he says he is priestly serving God’s gospel to them, so that they may be offered as sanctified in the Spirit.

“So I have boasting in Christ Jesus in things toward God. For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has worked through me for the obedience of the nations, by word and deed, by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fulfilled the gospel of Christ.”

He says he boasts in Christ Jesus, and calls that boast toward God. How can anyone doubt that it is not merely human for Christ to work marvels among the holy apostles by the Spirit’s power? Just as each of us does his own works by his own power, so also Christ, using the Spirit as his own power, works the marvels through the holy ones’ hand. Then how is he not God? For the Holy Spirit is not alien to him.

“All the churches of Christ greet you.” Yet elsewhere, writing to Timothy, he says: “so that you may know how one ought to behave in the house of God.” If he knows and attests the churches as Christ’s, then Christ is God.
“The God of peace will crush Satan under your feet quickly.” Peace is said to be God’s — for Christ said somewhere to the holy apostles: “My peace I give to you; my peace I leave
notes_covered: Christ works wonders by his own Spirit — not an alien Spirit.

title: Christ gives his peace; church of God; crucified Christ preached
english: to you.” Then how is the giver of peace not truly God, giving it to the worthy as his own good?
From the First Letter to the Corinthians.

“Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and brother Sosthenes, to the church of God.” Notice: after saying to the Romans, “All the churches of Christ greet you,” when he writes to the Corinthians he says the church is God’s.

“I mean this: each of you says, ‘I belong to Paul,’ or ‘I belong to Apollos,’ or ‘I belong to Cephas,’ or ‘I belong to Christ.’ Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized into Paul’s name?” So if Christ has not been divided, all things are his and all are his. And if he himself was crucified for us, and we were baptized into his name, we clearly owe ourselves to him. And we belong not to one human among us, but to God. Therefore Christ, the one over us, is God.

“Since Jews ask for a sign and Greeks seek wisdom, we proclaim Christ crucified — a stumbling block to Jews and folly to Greeks.” Would not anyone at all confess that the gospel proclamation calls people across the whole earth to true knowledge of God? Then how, or from where, is this doubtful? How, then, do the mystagogues proclaim Christ crucified? As one of us who endured death on a cross, so that the world’s faith is practiced toward a human? By no means. We have believed in the living God and
notes_covered: Faith of the world is not toward a mere human.

title: Crucified Christ is God’s testimony; Lord of glory
english: — the true one. So he knows the crucified Christ as God, and he proclaims him to the world, persuaded that he does not err.

“And I, when I came to you, brothers, did not come with superiority of speech or wisdom announcing to you the testimony of God. For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”

See how clearly, when he says he announces “the testimony of God” to the world, he added “Christ Jesus, and him crucified.” Therefore Christ Jesus, who endured the cross for us, is God. And his testimony is announced to the world through the holy apostles not in superiority of worldly speech and wisdom, but as in the Spirit’s power.

“Yet among the mature we speak wisdom — not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age who are being abolished — but we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom that God predetermined before the ages for our glory, which none of the rulers of this age knew. For if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

If Christ’s mystery is God’s wisdom and is proclaimed to the world, yet — as some somehow think — he is not truly God and faith is toward him anyway, how is the mystery wise if it carries people on earth away from true knowledge of God and turns the world into worship of a human? That is not the truth. The mystery is wise because it brings the straying near to God. Therefore Christ is God, and the crucified one is rightly called Lord of glory.
“According to the grace of God given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it.”
notes_covered: Against reducing the crucified to a mere human object of world-worship.

title: Christ the only foundation; temple of God by his Spirit
english: “For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that lies there, which is Jesus Christ.” If we have been propped on Christ as on a foundation, and are built on him through faith, and he himself is the security of all, how would he not be truly God — the one in whom are all things, and toward whom is the faith of all? Not as one of our kind — for we have not served a creature — but as God by nature and in truth.

“Do you not know that you are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person. For God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.” If by receiving Christ’s Spirit we are called God’s temple, how is he not truly God, the one through whom we are temples of God?

“So do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will also bring to light the hidden things of darkness and disclose the plans of hearts; and then praise will come to each from God.”

We expect our Lord Jesus Christ to come down from heaven in due times, and we shall all stand before him as he judges what is hidden and discloses the plans of hearts. And we are fully persuaded he will also praise the righteous; for to those standing on the right he will say: “Come, you blessed of my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.” So when he says that, while Christ praises, praise comes to each from God, how is he not clearly God?
“Or do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and you are not your own? For you were bought with a price; so glorify God in

title: Bought by his blood; one Lord; church of God is Christ’s
english: “in your body.” If by receiving Christ’s Spirit we have become temples of God, and we are not our own — bought by his blood, so that we no longer live for ourselves but for the one who bought us — how is Christ not clearly God, the one through whom we are temples of God, and whom we serve as God?

“About eating food offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one. For even if there are so-called gods in heaven or on earth — as indeed there are many gods and many lords — yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we for him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through him.”

If God alone is one and there is no other beside him, and the one Jesus Christ — through whom are all things — is taken together into the one nature of the deity, then he who is thought divinely in the Father’s same substance is God, even when he has been named Jesus Christ after being born of a woman. Note also: after naming him Christ Jesus, Paul says all things came to be through him, as of one Son according to the economic union.
“I became,” he says, “as without law to those without law — not being without God’s law, but under Christ’s law.” If the one who has Christ’s law has God’s law, how is Christ not God?
“Give no offense to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God.” Note that when he calls the church God’s, he again knows it as Christ’s.

“I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.” Blessed Luke, composing Christ’s genealogy for us, begins from Joseph, then, having reached

title: Christ head as Creator; Spirit gifts prove his deity
english: to Adam, he adds, “of God,” setting the God who made him as the human’s beginning. In the same way we say Christ is every man’s head: for man was made through him and brought into being — the Son not creating him as a mere under-worker, but rather in a God-working way, as Creator by nature.

The man is head of the woman because she was taken from his flesh and has him as her beginning. Likewise God is head of Christ because the Word is from him by nature — for the Word has been begotten from God the Father. Then how is Christ not God, whose head by nature is the Father? And when I say “Christ,” I mean the Word from God who has appeared in human form.

“Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, ‘Jesus be cursed,’ and no one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except in the Holy Spirit. There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; varieties of ministries, but the same Lord; and varieties of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.”

If saying that Christ is not God by nature and in truth is nothing other than saying “Jesus be cursed,” then those who cast him out from being God according to the truth are not doing this in the Holy Spirit. And if Paul says the varieties of gifts are at one time worked by the Spirit, at another by the same Lord, at another by the same God, he knows Christ to be God — the one who works as God through the Spirit, and who as Lord by nature distributes the gifts from above with authority as he wills. Remember also that Paul said Christ worked in him by the power of the Holy Spirit.
notes_covered: θεουργικῶς / ὑπουργικῶς: Son creates as natural Creator.

title: Christ sets church gifts; anathema on those who split the one Lord
english: “And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing.” Though these are said to be God’s doing, it is Christ who worked them. For he himself appointed the apostles in the church, and teachers as well, and worked powers; for he gave the holy disciples authority to heal every disease and every weakness among the people.

“The greeting is in my own hand — Paul’s. If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be anathema. Maranatha.” Whom, then, does he call Lord here? The Son himself is confessedly Lord, and likewise the Spirit — “for the Lord,” he says, “is the Spirit.” But blessed Paul’s aim in these words stretches toward Jesus himself; for there is, he says, one Lord, Jesus Christ.

So he anathematizes the one who does not love him. And the one who does not love him is the one who will not say he is Son of God by nature and in truth, but sets him in a second rank beside the Word from God, and wrongs the mystery of the economy by cutting the one Lord Jesus Christ into two.

From the Second Letter to the Corinthians: “But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and through us spreads the fragrance of the knowledge of him in every place; for we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing.”

Then how is Christ not God, if he himself is the fragrance of the knowledge of the Father? No one would learn the sweet scent of the divine nature from human nature alone. Just as the scent of humanity points to a human, so the scent of deity points to God. And if Christ is said to be — and truly is — the Father’s aroma,
notes_covered: Against splitting the one Lord into two.

title: Christ’s letter written by his own Spirit; veil lifted in the Lord
english: how is Christ not God, even if the Word from God the Father has become human economically?

“You are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by all people, and you show that you are a letter of Christ delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of fleshy hearts.”

God said somewhere through one of the holy prophets: “In that time, says the Lord, I will put my laws into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts.” So we have become Christ’s letter — he writing on us what he wills not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God — not merely as a minister, but, so to speak, by his own working; for the Spirit is his own. Then how is he not God, who writes for us in his own Spirit the way of knowing God?

About the Jews he says: “But their minds were hardened. For until this day the same veil remains unlifted at the reading of the old covenant, because it is abolished in Christ. But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart. But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”

If Christ is the end of the law and the prophets, and the veil over the reading of the old covenant is not uncovered except in Christ alone, what sense is there in thinking him a common human, honored only with the title of sonship? It turns out
notes_covered: Own Spirit = God writing the way of knowing God.

title: Gospel of Christ’s glory; image of God; judgment seat of Christ
english: that the end of our faith would then be not toward God but toward one of our kind — which is among the most absurd things.

“And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing, in whom the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that they may not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.”

If, as some think, Christ is a common human, joined to the Word from God only by a conjunction of face — for that is how they themselves speak — how is his gospel veiled among those who perish? The nations are disposed not as if he were God, but as if he were a human like us. And how have those who say about a human that he is human been blinded by Satan? What illumination is there in Christ’s gospel if he is not God, and is not glorified as being that? And how would he be the image of God if he reaches only as far as humanity, not truly being Son and God?

“Therefore we are ambitious, whether at home or away, to be well-pleasing to him. For we must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive what is due for the things done through the body, whether good or worthless.”

If the holy ones’ whole zeal is to please God, and we are ambitious to appear such to Christ while refusing to please humans, how is Christ not clearly God? And if he himself will judge the world — one lawgiver and judge being spoken of — it is plain that by this too he is God, even though the Word became flesh.
notes_covered: Against face-conjunction only; Christ as image and judge.

title: Live for the one who died; ambassadors of Christ; Spirit of Christ
english: “For the love of Christ constrains us, having concluded this: that one died for all, therefore all died; and he died for all so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and was raised for them.”

If we are all one, and we pray to live for him — making our life solemn by needing to fulfill his will — and we live for Christ, how would he not be God, the one to whom we are indebted and for whom we are eager to live, as the one who died for us and bought us all with his own blood?

“Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were appealing through us; we beg on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.” Notice: they are ambassadors for Christ, and they say God appeals to us. Then again they say, “We beg on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.” Therefore Christ is God; when we have been reconciled to him, we have been reconciled to God.
“But in everything we commend ourselves as servants of God.” Those called servants of God are also called servants of Christ; therefore Christ is God.

“For we are the temple of the living God, as God said: I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” If we are temples of the living God because the Spirit dwells in us — and that Spirit is also said to be Christ’s (“for if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him”) — how is Christ not God?
“destroying arguments and every high thing raised against the knowledge of God, and taking captive
notes_covered: Bought with his own blood; ambassadors for Christ = for God.

title: Captive every thought; Word emptied; Gal 2 died to law for Christ
english: “…taking every thought captive to the obedience of Christ.” How shall we demolish every high thing raised against the knowledge of God? How shall we take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ? For the Word emptied himself willingly, and became obedient to the Father as far as death.

So whenever some, from things done or said economically because of the flesh and the human, exalt themselves against the knowledge of the Son — saying that the one in human form is not true God and Son by nature — then we will demolish every high thing that is raised, overturning the opinions of those who choose to think that way, and turning every thought toward the economy of obedience. For the Son who has come within the measures of humanity must not refuse the human things.

From Galatians: “For through the law I died to the law, that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.”

What, then, does the inspired Paul mean here? A law was set by God through the voice of the prophets, and it was this: “The righteous shall live by faith.” A law was also set through Moses. So having followed the law of faith, he says, I died to the law through Moses — no longer working the things marked out for the ancients as in shadow and types. For that is what it means to die to the Mosaic law: that we may live to God, clinging to faith in Christ.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Faith better than Moses’ law; Spirit given through Christ; pedagogue to Christ
english: Preferring the justification in Christ to the law through Moses, how is Christ not God — the one through whom the law is abolished, since his faith surpasses it? And if Christ were merely a human being, how could faith in him have become better than the law?

“He who supplies the Spirit to you and works powers…” The law through Moses, though it is God’s law and “spoken through angels,” does not have the supply of the Holy Spirit, nor did it procure for anyone the power to work wonders. But through faith in Christ we gain both. How then is faith in him not better, if it has abolished the old law? And if we who live by faith are in a better state than those of the time when the law held, how is Christ not God?

“Before faith came we were kept under the law, shut up for the faith about to be revealed… that we might be justified by faith. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian; for you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.”

If the law was a guardian pointing to none other than Christ alone — even while teaching true knowledge of God — how is Christ not God? And if the law is abolished through faith in him and hands him the end of its guardianship, leading those under it to the highest good — and that final good is nothing other than knowledge of the true God — how could anyone doubt that he is God?
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Baptized into Christ; boast in the cross; seated at the right hand; Christ in the heart
english: But we are baptized into Father and Son and Holy Spirit — so how have we been baptized into Christ if he is not true Son, though there is one Son by nature? Yet we have been baptized into him. Therefore he is God as one Son and one Lord according to the economic union, the Word having become flesh.

“But then, not knowing God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods; now that you know God — or rather are known by God — how can you turn again to the weak and beggarly elements?” If we have come to know God by confessing Christ, and say we have been known by God as known to him, how is Christ not God?

“But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.” Blessed David sings, “I will boast in God my Savior.” The saying is wise and holy: we ought not to glory in a human being, but in God. How then does Paul say he boasts in the cross of Christ? He ought rather to do that in God. Yet the Spirit-bearer boasts in the death of Christ; so he knows him to be true God who suffered for us in the flesh.

From Ephesians, concerning God the Father: “according to the working of the might of his strength, which he worked in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above every rule and authority…” See: the Father has seated the one raised from the dead at his right hand. Does a human as we are, and nothing more, sit with the nature above all things? Or — what is true — is he God who became human, consubstantial with the Father insofar as he shone forth from him, and who took on the human economically, and is for that reason crowned with divine glory?

“Therefore remember that you once Gentiles in the flesh… that at that time you were without Christ… having no hope and without God in the world.” If the nations, while they did not have Christ, remained in atheism before the world, and once they have him they are no longer without God, how then is Christ not God?

“For this reason I bow my knees before the Father… that he may grant you… to be strengthened through his Spirit in the inner human being, that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts.” The name Christ Jesus, as we have often said, everywhere signifies the Word who shone forth from God in human form. How then does he dwell in our hearts through faith unless he is understood as God — the Word having united the flesh to himself, who also dwells in us in a divine way?
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Christ dwells by the Spirit; surpassing knowledge of Christ; Colossians mystery
english: Who is the one who dwells in you? Or how is he housed in human beings through faith? Yet John says clearly about God: “By this we know that he is in us: that he has given us of his Spirit.”

From Philippians, on the boasts that are in the law: “Whatever gains I had, these I have counted as loss because of Christ. Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as refuse, in order that I may gain Christ.”

Why are the things in the law loss and refuse? And what is the surpassing worth of the knowledge of Jesus Christ? The law through Moses proclaimed the true God by nature to those of old, while the mystagogues of the new covenant have announced Christ to the world. But if he is a human as we are — merely common, not believed to be God by hypostatic union with the Word from God — how will faith according to him surpass the faith of the law?

From Colossians: “Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church, of which I became a minister according to the stewardship of God given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God — the mystery hidden from the ages and from the generations, but now revealed to his saints, to whom God willed to make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Colossians mystery; walk in Christ; Word became flesh; door of the word
english: “…Christ in you, the hope of glory, whom we proclaim.” How is the mystery hidden, or how is it God’s word at all, and what riches of glory are in it, if Christ is merely a common human as we are? The mystery is neither great nor worth naming unless we approach Christ as God and understand that the Word, being God and in the equality and form of the Father, lowered himself into emptying — becoming human and remaining what he was. Only so is the mystery thought rich and full of glory.

“As therefore you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in faith.” How did we receive Christ? Wise John will teach it: “And the Word became flesh.” Yet he has not ceased to be Word even though he became flesh; even so he sits with his own Father, and the crucified one is named Lord of glory.

“Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching in it with thanksgiving, praying also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of God for which I am also in bonds, that I may make it clear as I ought to speak.” If Christ is not God but only a human honored by divine grace, there is nothing deep in the mystery about him. What door would he need for making it plain and speaking as one ought? There is nothing great or hard in saying about a human that he is human by nature. But if the Word from God is proclaimed as having become human, then we need God himself — the one who opens the door and grants us to speak the mystery in the fitting way.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Hebrews: firstborn worshiped; angels spirits; throne forever; anointed as man
english: From Hebrews: “And when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says: Let all the angels of God worship him.” The Word from God the Father is named only-begotten by nature, because he alone has been begotten from the Father alone. He is also called firstborn when he entered the world as one who had become human and part of it. Yet even so he is worshiped by the holy angels — and worship is reserved and fitting for God alone. How, then, is Christ not God, the one worshiped even in heaven?

“Of the angels he says: He makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire; but of the Son: Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.”

If the one who holds a throne forever is the maker of angels — having loved righteousness and hated lawlessness, and for that reason said to be anointed with the oil of gladness by God the Father — what thoughts should we form about him? If he makes his angels spirits and holds a throne of deity, how is he anointed with the oil of gladness? So he creates angels as God, and is anointed as human — not into the nature of deity, but into the skilled economy of the anointing.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: God and man economically; living God; blood of Christ cleanses; trampling the Son
english: So Christ is God and human: God by nature, and the same one human as we are economically, when he came to be from a woman according to the flesh.

“See to it, brothers, that there not be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in falling away from the living God.” By denying Christ we fall away from the living and true God; by remaining in faith toward him we in no way make that apostasy. How, then, is Christ not God?

“For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the purity of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” If Christ is not true God, what is the benefit through his blood? Or how will he cleanse our conscience from dead works? What more does the blood of a common human have than the blood of goats? Nothing at all — except that one is of an irrational animal and the other of a rational one. But since the one who is from God by nature took flesh and laid down his own blood for all, by that very fact he can cleanse those who believe in him, free them from dead works, and lead them into worship of God.

“Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without mercy on the evidence of two or three witnesses. How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant a common thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace by which he was sanctified?” The one who insults — that is, sets aside — a divine law does not face a charge equal to sinning against a human, but one far heavier.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Christ’s blood not common; speaker from heaven; same yesterday and forever
english: So the one who has broken the law has fallen under the sentence of death, while the one who has wronged a human might even be worthy of pardon. How, then, is the one who counted Christ’s blood a common thing under a worse sentence than the one who sins against Moses’ law? Yet he is under a worse one — and very fittingly. Christ’s blood is not common, then: for the Word was God, having become flesh.

“See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. For if they did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, much less will we escape if we turn away from the one who warns from heaven, whose voice then shook the earth, but now he has promised: Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.” Who is the one who warned on earth, whom the fathers of the Jews refused and so were put in danger? Clearly Moses. But Christ is not from earth; rather from the heavens. For the God Word from above and from the Father became human — and is God. So the sentence is worse for those who turn away from him, and very fittingly. As wise John says: “He who is of the earth speaks from the earth” — that is, human things — “but he who comes from above is above all,” as God, of course. And that is what Christ was and is.

“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” We will find the Word sprung from God called Jesus Christ when he became human from a woman. How, then, is he the same yesterday and today and forever? Clearly by union with the Word from God into one Son, the flesh assumed by him being understood with him. For so the Word’s unchangeableness by nature remains for him even when he is understood with the flesh.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Timothy: Savior name; Titus: appearing of our great God and Savior
english: From Timothy: “Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Savior, to Timothy, my true child in faith.” The name Savior fits no one else properly and truly — except the one who is God by nature. So the mystagogue has named him that even here. Yet our Lord Jesus Christ is also Savior: he is named Jesus, and the blessed angel made the force of the name clear: “You shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” So Christ is God, if he is Savior of all people, as the inspired Paul says.

From Titus: “For the saving grace of God has appeared to all people, training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires and to live soberly, justly, and godly in the present age, awaiting the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works.”

What grace has appeared to us, or of what God — though it is called saving for all people? Clearly “the Lord, being God, has also appeared to us,” as blessed David says. We await his appearing of glory from the heavens. And he himself is our great God and Savior, Jesus the Christ, who has given himself for us so that, freeing us from all sin, he may present to himself genuine worshipers.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: James: every good gift; submit to God; Peter greeting and blood sprinkling
english: Then who will say Emmanuel is not true God, when blessed Paul speaks of him as “our great God and Savior Jesus Christ”?

From the catholic letters — James — that Christ is God: “Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers. Every good gift and every perfect present is from above, coming down from the Father of lights.” Every gift is good; and the good gift is the Holy Spirit, and the power to work the signs of God in him. So if Christ grants the Spirit to the saints, and also the power to work wonders, how would Christ not be true God?

“Submit therefore to God; resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Clearly here he said we must submit to God. But Christ says: “Take my yoke upon you.” So when those who take his yoke are not submitting to someone other than God, how would he not be God?

From Peter’s letter: “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect sojourners of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace be multiplied.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Sanctified by his Spirit and blood; new birth hope; Spirit of Christ in prophets
english: See: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father he named himself an apostle of Christ. Explaining the manner of that apostleship, he says it was done “in sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ.” So when those who believe in him are sanctified by the Spirit, and he also sprinkles us with his blood for cleansing, how would the one who sanctifies with his own Spirit and cleanses believers with his blood not be understood as God? For God was in flesh.

“Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has begotten us anew to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven.” If God begot us to a living and abiding hope, and Christ has done this through his own resurrection from the dead, how would he not be God?

“Concerning this salvation the prophets who prophesied of the grace that would come to you searched and inquired, inquiring what person or time the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating.” See again: here the Holy Spirit is called Christ’s, though he is God’s. So Christ is God, as one who has the Holy Spirit as his own.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Bought by Christ’s blood; true God and eternal life; Jude: denying the Master
english: From Peter’s letter: “There were also false prophets… who will bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them.” For we were bought at a price “not with perishable things, silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ.” So we belong to the one who purchased us, even while we serve the living and true God. How, then, is Christ not God — the one we have enrolled as Master, and know as living and true?

“And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true one, and we are in the true one, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.” Jesus Christ is not understood as the Word from God the Father naked, by himself, and outside flesh; but when he became human, then he was also named Christ Jesus. So when he himself is the true God and the eternal life, who among those who think otherwise will put up with it?

From Jude: “While I was making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write appealing to you to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints. For certain people have crept in… who pervert the grace of our God into sensuality and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.” How does someone who once believed deny our Lord Jesus Christ? We have received the word of the incarnation. But if we say that the Son who is the Word from God the Father is one, and another is…
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: One Lord by economic union; Matthew: born of Spirit, saves his people
english: If we take the one from the woman as a separate person, we have denied the only Master. For there is one Lord Jesus Christ by an economic union — I mean with the Word from God — his flesh ascending into the glory of the deity. So there is one Christ and Son; and so he will be Master of all.

From Matthew’s Gospel — that Christ is God: “While he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying: Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife, for what is begotten in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”

In the same breath he sets down two things proper to God, and not fitting for human nature. Of the one born from Mary he said that those saved through him are his own people, and that he himself will also free them from sins. All things belong to God, and to him alone it would befit to be able to free sinners from sins. So the one begotten from the holy virgin is God, whose own people we are; and he has freed us from sins, as one who has authority for that too.

“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea.” In Bethlehem of Judea has been born the one from the root of Jesse. And God the Father says about him through one of the prophets: “And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are by no means least among the thousands of Judah; for from you shall come forth for me one to be ruler in Israel, and his goings forth are from the beginning, from the days of eternity.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Eternal goings-forth; baptize in Spirit; leper; demons; harvest Lord
english: How, then, is the one born in Bethlehem of Judea said to have goings forth from the beginning of the age — that is, the beginning of existence — though he was born in the last times of the age? So Christ is God, and what is most ancient of the Word of God would befit him. For he was God, and for our sake endured a fleshly birth from a woman.

“I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who comes after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor.” We deny that baptizing in the Holy Spirit is a work of mere humanity; nor do we say the intelligible threshing floor — that is, those on the earth — belongs to a mere human. All things are God’s, and to him alone it befits to be able to baptize believers in the Holy Spirit. Yet Christ, who comes after John according to the flesh, has done this; and he also clears his own floor. So he is true God.

“And behold, a leper came and worshiped him, saying: Lord, if you will, you can make me clean. And stretching out his hand he touched him, saying: I will; be clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.” To be able to work in a way proper to God is not a human property; it would follow rather the nature beyond all things alone. Working thus, Christ is not a bare human as we are, but rather God in human form. So also understand the healing of Peter’s mother-in-law, and when he is seen rebuking winds and sea.

“And the demons begged him, saying: If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs. And he said to them: Go.” Whose work is it to provide for all things and save them, if not the one who is God by nature alone? See what providence over beings Christ exercised: unclean demons were not even allowed authority over a herd of pigs.

“Then he says to his disciples: The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest. And calling his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Lord of the harvest sends apostles; confess before the Father; come to me
english: He knows that the Lord of the harvest is the God of all: the intelligible threshing floor — that is, humanity — is his, and the harvest is his. Yet see: having ordered them to pray the Lord of the harvest, he immediately showed that he himself is that Lord, sending out the laborers — the holy apostles — and giving them authority over unclean spirits as God. For it is not within the measures of humanity to give anyone the working of the Holy Spirit; yet Christ has given it. How, then, is he not God by nature and in truth, even though the Word has become flesh?

“Everyone who confesses me before humans, I also will confess before my Father in heaven; and whoever denies me before humans, I also will deny before my Father in heaven.” Many of the saints have been called to the glory of martyrdom and perfected through sufferings and death, confessing Christ. Were they crowned for insisting he is a common human, or rather for honoring him as God in their confessions? The answer is clear. Those who denied this also slipped from the glory of martyrdom, and on the day of judgment they will find Christ himself denying them. How, then, is he not God — the one who crowns with martyrdom’s glory those who truly confess that he is this?
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you.” If Emmanuel is not truly God, how does he lay his own yoke on us?
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: His yoke; greater than the temple; cast out demons in Jesus’ name; angels of the Son
english: For all things are servants of God. The law too is called a yoke. Yet Christ lays his own yoke on us and subjects us to himself, even while bearing all things under the Father: so he is God. Hence he also claims that all things lie under him.

“Or have you not read in the law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are guiltless? But I say to you that something greater than the temple is here.” If priests who profane the sabbath are guiltless because they offer services to God, how is service of Christ understood as greater than what is done in the temple? Clearly those under the law served in shadow and copy of the heavenly things, while the inspired disciples who attended and ministered to Christ had the greater glory. And if ministering to Christ stands in better things than the worship under the law, how would he not be understood as truly God?

“If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.” If the disciples have healed the demonized in Christ’s name — for they cried out, “In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene” — how would he not be understood as true God? A mere human’s glory and power would not have been enough to overpower Satan.

“Just as the weeds are collected and burned with fire, so will it be at the end of the age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will collect out of his kingdom all causes of sin and those who do lawlessness.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Son of Man sends his angels; Peter’s confession; temple tax setup
english: “…all causes of sin and those who do lawlessness, and they will throw them into the furnace of fire.” Of God it is written: “Bless the Lord, all his angels.” For an angel is not a human’s servant; rather, all things belong to God. How, then, does he say of the Son of Man that he will send his angels? So he is God, as one who has the angels as his own and is served through the spirits above.

Christ asked: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” And Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus answered him: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father in heaven.” If Christ were a bare human, why is Peter marvelled at for confessing him? How is he God-taught, or what illumination from above did he need to learn the mystery about him? But he knew him to be God, and confessed him Son of the living God — and for that he is marvelled at. Yet he says one Son, not two sons; so it is impious to divide him into two.
“For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels.” See again: he calls the spirits above his angels, though he is called Son of Man.
“When they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax approached Peter and said: Does your teacher not pay the two-drachma? He said: Yes.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Sons free of the tax; Hosanna to David’s son; throne with all angels
english: “…tolls or census? From their sons or from strangers?” He said: “From strangers.” Jesus said to him: “Then the sons are free.” How does he say he is free, outside the law, untaxed, and truly Son, unless he is God who has shared flesh and blood by hypostatic union? Yet he paid the two-drachma, as the Son above the law who has come under the law. As a mere human he would not be understood as above the law. How could he? He would not have freedom by nature unless he is understood as God in human form.

As our Savior Christ of all was going up to Jerusalem, children went before him, praising and saying: “Hosanna to the son of David.” The doxology is wholly God-befitting. The Pharisees were indignant and came saying: “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them: “Yes; have you never read: From the mouth of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise?” Here we must recall blessed David: “O Lord, our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth, for your majesty is exalted above the heavens. From the mouth of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise.” The children praised, saying “Hosanna to the son of David,” and he accepts the doxology as one praised. Blessed David did not ascribe this to a common human, but rather to the Lord, whose name has become wondrous in all the earth; for the majesty too was exalted above the heavens. How, then, is the son of David according to the flesh — Christ — not God?
“When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.”
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Judge of the world; seated at the right hand; creation shakes at the cross
english: Will Christ sit as one human among us, with all the angels standing by him, and so judge the world? What sense would that make? For it is written that “there is one lawgiver and judge.” So Christ is God — the one who has God’s glory and a throne, angels standing by, and who judges the inhabited world in righteousness.

“And the high priest said to him: I adjure you by the living God to tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God. Jesus says to him: You have said so; yet I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.” How does the Son of Man sit at the right hand of Power? Clearly: even if the Word from God has become Son of Man, he has not ceased to be God, but is the same one who sits with the One who begot him, and is seen shining in the dignities of the deity, even though he has become flesh.

“And Jesus, crying with a loud voice, gave up the spirit. And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook, and the rocks were split, and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.” If Christ were a common human, how was there such uproar in the elements when he died? The sun drew in its ray and made darkness in daytime; the earth, seeing her own Master insulted by the Jews, was split; and Hades too released the souls of the saints.
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: God in flesh; knows hearts; salvation from the Jews; ask in my name
english: Who is doing these things? Is it not God? For God was in flesh, and the creation was in a way angered together with him when he was insulted.

From John’s Gospel: “But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew all people, and because he had no need that anyone should testify about the human; for he himself knew what was in the human.” Of God it is written that “he who alone forms their hearts”; and he himself says something similar. So if he knows all things and knows what is in the human, how would he not be God as the one who searches hearts and kidneys?

“You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.” Do you hear that he says salvation is from the Jews? Yet we have enrolled God as Savior. For he has saved us “not an elder, not an angel, but the Lord himself,” according to the Scriptures. He is named Christ Jesus, having come to be from the Jews according to the flesh; and Jesus is interpreted “salvation.” So he himself is the salvation from the Jews. Therefore even if the Word has become flesh and has taken hold of Abraham’s seed, he is God also with the flesh.

“Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes in me will also do the works that I do, and greater works than these he will do, because I am going to my Father. And whatever you ask in my name, I will do.” He says he is going to the Father, though the Son exists as God by nature and is himself the one who fills all things. So he goes in a human way…
notes_covered: True deity of the incarnate Son.

title: Ask in my name; Father and Son give as one God
english: …for he was taken up into heaven. But as God he promises to fulfill the requests of those who pray, if they make their petitions in his name. Then: to whom would it be more fitting to fulfill the prayers of the saints and grant their requests, except to the one who alone is by nature and truly God?

“You did not choose me, but I chose you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he will give you.” See how everywhere he shows that he works the same things with authority as God the Father. For he had said, “If you ask in my name, I will do it”; but now he says, “Whatever you ask the Father in my name he will give you.” So then — does the Father give on his own apart from the Son, and the Son separately give his share apart from the Father? Would the saints’ prayer-requests then come from two gods? Not so — God forbid. For there is one God, the Father, and one Lord Jesus Christ. The Father distributes the good things in the Son, in the Spirit. Yet the asking in prayer is in Christ Jesus, and the Lord Jesus who became human is understood as the one who is also named Word.

“And on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly I say to you, if you ask my Father anything, he will give it to you in my name. Ask and you will receive, that your joy may be full.” This too will sit briefly in the same sense as what is above, and what follows likewise. It runs thus: “On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father…”
notes_covered: Father and Son give as one God, not two.

title: Eternal life is knowing Father and Christ; glory and oneness
english: “…the Father loves you, because you have loved me, because I came forth from the Father.”

“And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.” If knowledge of Jesus Christ is necessarily joined to, and enters together with, knowledge of the only true God, and this procures eternal life, how is it not clear to all that Christ is true God? For the Word became flesh, and remained Word.

“That the world may believe that you sent me; and the glory that you have given me I have given them, that they may be one as we are one; I in them and you in me, that they may be perfected into one.” Setting the eye of understanding carefully on the force of what is before us, let us consider what is in it. What glory does the Son say he has received from the Father and given to us? He himself will free us from searching this out when he says “that they may be one as we are one.” For in natural identity the Word from God is one with his own Father, even if each is understood in his own hypostasis. And how has he also come to be in us? In the same way — I mean essentially and naturally? Yet God’s nature would be wholly incompatible with creation, I mean in identity according to essence. How then has the One above creation come to be in us naturally? He became human, so that just as he is one with the Father in the nature of the deity, so he may also become one with us in the relation according to humanity; for in this way we too are perfected into one.
notes_covered: Word became flesh and remained Word; oneness via humanity.

title: Locked doors; Spirit breathed; forgive and retain sins
english: “…gathered for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and says to them: Peace to you.” Someone might reasonably raise this puzzle: if the Word was in a body even after the resurrection, as also before the precious cross, how did he appear unexpectedly in the midst of the disciples when the doors were locked? To this we say: by divine power. One must remember Paul saying that “from now on we know no one according to the flesh; even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no longer.” For after the rising from the dead, since the economy on which the taking of flesh was done as needed is already finished, he uses authority and power befitting God, wanting to be recognized rather through these than through the measures of the emptying, as at the fitting time.

“And having said this he breathed on them and says to them: Receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain those of any, they are retained.” The whole deed is God-befitting and worthy of every word. First, breathing on the apostles and giving the Spirit is not a human act. Then it is great and above creation to grant such authority that they may retain the sins of those they choose, and also forgive those they may wish. And why does he give the Spirit also through a fleshly breath? Because his flesh has not become alien to the Word, but is his own in a proper sense. The breathing through flesh is human; but it is the work of divine power to make those who are counted worthy sharers of the Spirit.
notes_covered: Locked doors by divine power; Spirit through own flesh.

title: Baptist prepares the Lord’s way; David’s throne forever — Christ is God
english: From Luke’s Gospel. An angel of God says to Zechariah about the holy Baptist: “And there will be joy and gladness for you, and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord, and he will drink no wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb, and he will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.”

And when asked by the Jews, “Who are you?” he says: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.” And Zechariah himself, prophesying over his own child, says: “And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins.” For he went ahead of Christ, and became his forerunner, and proclaimed that the ways were to be prepared for him, and prophesied the word concerning him, turning people as toward God who is able to justify those in sins. Then — how is Christ not God?

“This one will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” So then — shall we lie under one of those like us, ruled continuously and without end, or shall we rather be under God ruling us who are in Christ? And not as if some outside mediator were taken on for this, but as the God and Father holding sway over all things through the Son and in the Son? And if this is true, then Christ is God.
notes_covered: Baptist prepares the Lord’s way → Christ is God.
translator_notes: Luke lacunae filled from known gospel text where OCR truncated.

title: Annunciation, Baptist’s leap, Simeon’s salvation — Christ is God
english: Mary said to the angel: “How will this be for me, since I do not know a man?” And answering, the angel said to her: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one to be born will also be called Son of God.” So then — is the one born ineffably through the Spirit from the holy virgin only called Son, as if created, or is he believed to be Son by nature and truly, and God? This is true. So let the Word be understood as having become flesh hypostatically — that is, having made his own the flesh from the holy virgin through the Spirit. For in this way he will also be truly God.

“And when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and cried out with a loud voice and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And how is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?” When God works the gift of prophecy, someone becomes a prophet; in any other way, not at all. So when the greeting of the holy virgin Mary, still carrying Jesus, moved John in the womb into prophecy, how is Christ not God — who even in the virgin’s womb moved the Baptist in a God-befitting way into the power of prophecy?

“Now you dismiss your servant, Master, according to your word in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all the peoples, a light for revelation to the nations and glory of your people Israel.” Taking Jesus into his arms, Simeon says such things about him. So how is he salvation? And how a light for revelation to the nations — unless he is truly God and only Son by nature…
notes_covered: Hypostatic flesh; Baptist prophesies in womb; Simeon.

title: Same Word from Father and virgin; forgives sins; Isaiah’s signs
english: …from the Father as Word, and the same one from the virgin according to flesh? What revelation came to the nations, except that in him they knew that he is God, and by worshiping him they escaped the charge of worshiping a god other than the one who is by nature and truly God?

“And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, answered and said to them: Why do you reason in your hearts? Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you, or to say: Rise and walk? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins — he said to the paralyzed man: I say to you, rise, and taking up your bed go to your house.” If only the God of all frees us from offenses, this fitting no one else, and Christ also grants this with God-befitting authority, how would he not be God? For he is called Son of Man, born of a woman according to flesh, though the Word is God.

“In that hour he healed many of diseases and scourges and evil spirits, and to many blind he granted sight. And answering he said to them: Go tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind see again, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor are evangelized, and blessed is whoever is not scandalized in me.” Showing himself by the works themselves as the accomplisher of God-befitting mighty deeds, Christ brings to mind what was said through the prophets’ voice about him. So the blessed Isaiah said: “Strengthen weak hands and knees…”

title: Isaiah: our God comes; Christ rebukes wind and sea
english: “…paralyzed.” Then almost stretching out a hand he points to Emmanuel, saying thus: “Behold our God; behold the Lord comes with strength, and his arm with lordship.” And he said also elsewhere that “Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear. Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the stammerers will be clear,” and still further: “The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised; for the dew from you is healing to them.” And again he spoke in his person: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me; he has sent me to evangelize the poor, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind.” So when he makes the prophets’ voices the sign — that is, the proof — of faith in himself, and the prophets proclaim him God, who would dare to say the opposite of these things?

The disciples, he says, were being storm-tossed on the lake; then “coming they woke him saying: Master, we are perishing. And having been woken he rebuked the wind and the surge of the water, and it ceased and there was a calm.” It has been said about Christ through the voice of the blessed David: “You rule the might of the sea; you calm the tossing of its waves; the heavens are yours, and the earth is yours; you founded the inhabited world and its fullness.” So what would fit the one who calms the sea if not also to rule all things? And to have the heavens as his own, and to be able to found the inhabited world and its fullness — how would Christ not be understood to be truly God, the one who rebukes sea and winds, and that with authority?

title: Gerasene: Christ is the God who acted; girl sleeps to God; servant among them
english: “And the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to be with him. But he sent him away saying: Return to your house, and tell how much God has done for you. And he went away proclaiming through the whole city how much God had done for him.” In the country of the Gerasenes Christ healed the man fiercely demonized, who also begged to be with him. But though he had healed him and cast out the spirits, he ordered him to go to his house and proclaim how much God had done for him. So he himself worked as being true God. For we do not say somewhere that he became a minister of divine grace, like one of the prophets or of the holy apostles; rather he himself was crushing Satan by his own and God-befitting power. So in his name the demons were also subjected to the holy disciples, and they themselves confessed this.

About the synagogue ruler’s daughter Christ says: “Do not weep; for the girl did not die, but is sleeping.” So was he lying? Far from it — he speaks truth. And in what way? Because it is written: “He is not God of the dead, but of the living.” For they live to God who are going to live; therefore the dead are dead according to humans, but according to the life-giving nature — that is, the divine — they have not died. So he speaks truth as God when he says about the girl: “She did not die, but is sleeping.”

Speaking with his own disciples he said: “Who is greater, the one reclining or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am in your midst as the one who serves.” You see how he lowered himself from what befits the deity and the glory…
notes_covered: True God acting, not mere grace-minister.

title: Servant yet Master; right hand of Power; life-giving body and blood
english: …in the Master’s way he almost shakes off being thought of in a servant’s rank; yet he honors this because of the human. “For I am,” he says, “in your midst as the one who serves.” So even if he has come down among servants, he is still himself the one reclining — as Master, and served by all creation as God.

So Christ said to them — clearly to the chief priests of the Jews who were asking: “If you are the Christ, tell us. If I tell you, you will not believe; and if I ask, you will not answer. But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.” If the Son of Man sits at the right hand of God’s power, how is Christ not God — shining in the highest seats and sharing the Father’s throne? For a created nature does not sit with the God who is so by nature at all; yet the Son of Man does sit with him. So he is God by economic union, the Word born from God having become flesh.

That Christ is life and life-giving. From the letter to the Corinthians: “I speak as to the wise; judge what I say. The cup of blessing that we bless — is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break — is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we the many are one body; for we all partake of the one bread.” Human flesh, as far as its own nature goes, would not be life-giving, nor would human blood if it were common and by itself; but Christ’s body and precious blood give life — and being able to give life belongs to God alone…
notes_covered: Right hand = God by union; eucharist life-giving.

title: Last Adam life-giving Spirit; image of the heavenly; incorruption
english: …in need of life. So Christ is God; for in this way his body will be life-giving. But if he is thought of as a human separately, honored only with the name of Christ and having a bare son’s person, how would his body be life-giving?

“The first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving spirit,” and again: “The first man is of the earth, dusty; the second man is the Lord from heaven. As the dusty one, so also those who are dusty; and as the heavenly one, so also those who are heavenly; and just as we have worn the image of the dusty, let us also wear the image of the heavenly. And this I say, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit God’s kingdom, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.” And he adds to these: “for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal put on immortality.” The first human became a living soul; for as a creature he needed the God who gives life. But the last Adam — that is, Christ — because he did not need life as God, became a life-giving spirit for us, which is a proper advantage of the divine nature. And the first is the dusty one from earth; but the second is from heaven, though born through a woman — for the Word from above and from heaven and from God the Father, even if he has become human, is no less from heaven. And if, held by corruption and death, we are for that reason said to have worn the dusty one’s image, when we put on incorruption we will wear the heavenly one’s image. And incorruption again is a proper good of the deity by nature. For the dead are changed, and the corruptible…
notes_covered: Last Adam needs no life; gives life-giving Spirit; incorruption = deity’s own.

title: Christ raises the dead as Life; shared flesh abolishes death
english: …is clothed with incorruption, the Only-begotten having become according to us, and transferring the mortal into immortality, and remaking the corruptible into incorruption in himself first; for in this way a road into life has also come to be for us ourselves.

From the second letter to the Corinthians: “But we ourselves,” he says, “have had the sentence of death in ourselves, so that we would not trust in ourselves but in the God who raises the dead.” If we say that raising the dead is most fitting to the God who is so by nature — because he is life and life-giving — and Christ said, “I am the resurrection and the life,” and he is also seen to have raised the dead, then he is God, as life by nature.

From the letter to the Hebrews: “Since then the children have shared blood and flesh, he himself likewise shared the same things, so that through death he might abolish the one who has the power of death — that is, the devil.” Likewise with whom? The Word from God has shared blood and flesh with those ranked among God’s children, so that by giving his own body to death he might make it alive again, existing as life itself by nature as God. For how has death’s power been abolished, unless the body that fell into death lived again — being the own body of the life by nature, that is, of the Word who is from God?
That Jesus Christ is one Son and Lord. From John’s first catholic letter.
notes_covered: Only-begotten remakes mortality; Word’s own body as Life.

title: Word of life handled; faith in Christ as faith in God
english: “What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we looked upon and our hands handled, concerning the word of life — and the life was manifested, and we have seen and testify and announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was manifested to us.” See: he says they have seen with eyes and even handled with hands the one who is from the beginning — that is, the Word from the Father, the eternal life — though according to his own nature the Word from the Father is invisible and untouchable; for what is bodiless is untouchable. But he says they have seen and handled the Word who has come to be in flesh. So there is one Son and God and Lord even if the Word has become flesh.

That faith toward Christ is as toward God. From Peter’s first letter: “So that,” he says, “your faith and hope may be in God” — and yet Christ is proclaimed through the holy apostles. And he himself says somewhere: “Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes in me has eternal life.” So when faith is toward God, and Christ says “Believe in me,” how would he not be God clearly?

From John’s first letter: “And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ.” If it is not against the Father’s will that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and faith is also practiced by us not as toward a mere human but as toward the living and true God — then Christ is God.
notes_covered: One Son as flesh; faith in Christ = God.

title: Confess the Word come in flesh; Jesus is the Only-begotten sent
english: “By this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God; and this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming, and now is already in the world.” So do we confess Jesus as a human and as one like us — or rather that the Word, being God, became flesh, not neglecting to be God, but rather remaining what he was even if he became human? This is not doubtful. So the one who does not say that Christ is truly God, but divides and shrinks his glory, will be caught having the spirit of the antichrist.

“And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world; whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God.” We say that the Son has been sent from God the Father — that is, the Only-begotten Word from him by nature — and that he was named Jesus when he also endured the birth according to flesh from a woman economically. So the Word from God became human. And if someone confesses him thus, he has God remaining in him, and he himself will also be in God; for God will remember him and will also count him as his own, as a sharer in him. But the one who does not confess that the Word from God the Father himself is Jesus — having lowered himself into humanity — would neither grow rich with God in him, nor himself be in God according to the mode of spiritual kinship.
“Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.” So the one who does not believe would not even be counted among children…

title: Children of God; water, blood, Spirit are one Son’s
english: …of God. For if as many as received the Son “he gave authority to become children of God,” as the evangelist says, those who have not received him would not be counted among God’s children, not having known the one through whom this exists.

“And who is the one who conquers the world if not the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ — not in the water only, but in the water and the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth. For there are three who testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three are the one.” The one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God conquers the world; and who Jesus is, the disciple himself makes clear to us saying: “This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ.” But he also speaks of blood and of Spirit, and says the three are the one. So the Word became flesh, and he sanctifies us by the Spirit, and cleanses by the blood, and washes again with clean water; and the Son is altogether one, whose we also say the Spirit and the water and the blood are.

“If we receive the testimony of humans, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, that he has testified about his Son. The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself; the one who does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that he has testified about his Son.” And the Father has testified to the Son through the Spirit and through a voice. For that he is his Son according to…
notes_covered: One Son: Spirit/water/blood; Word flesh sanctifies.

title: Jordan shows enfleshed Son; hand-touch proves natural union
english: …truth, his being able to supply the Spirit to the saints and to work powers through him would testify. And so he was saying: “That one will glorify me.” And he has also testified in another way; for he glorified him at the Jordan saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I have been well pleased.” So as many as, dividing, say that the one from a woman is not a true son, and refer the name of sonship only to the bare Word from God, make the Father a liar; for he showed the Word enfleshed at the Jordan, and then the Spirit also testified to him that he is both God and truly Son.

From Matthew’s Gospel.
